one_month_reasoning: No company catalyst is confirmed before Oct 31. Q3-26 results are unannounced: Q1/Q2 came May 13/Aug 12, MarketBeat estimates Nov 10 and TipRanks Oct 22 (unconfirmed), so I put ~15% on an in-window report. In-window drivers: (1) late-October hyperscaler Q3 reports (MSFT and META are anchor customers) reset AI-capex sentiment; (2) the 10-yr at 5.29%, +33bp in a week, weighs on long-duration, financing-heavy names; (3) neocloud credit is under strain (CoreWeave 2030 notes ~11.6% YTM, CDS ~855bp in July), so any new Nebius convert or ATM could repeat the -10% day of Aug 2026; up to 12.3M ATM shares remained at 6/30; (4) ~20% short interest adds squeeze risk on good news. No clear directional edge, so median ~$230 (slightly below spot for supply/dilution risk) with sigma 28%, about annual vol / 3.5.

fair_value.method: Blend of a site-by-site DCF $97 (40%: every inventory site once; Microsoft, Meta and Q2-26 contracts at contract terms discounted at 8.0-10.0%, everything else probability-weighted at WACC 12.1%; single-rate $93), EV/NTM EBITDA $200 (35%: 9x ~$10.2B) and EV/NTM sales $200 (25%: 4.5x ~$20.4B), giving ~$159 per share 12 months out. The split rate adds only ~$4 because contracts are short (5 yrs, fully run off by 2032) and the build blocks carry their own capex; the site rebuild nets to about -$7 on the DCF.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-by-site cohort FCFF model 2027-2050 + Gordon terminal (one 6-yr refresh cycle average). Every inventory site appears once (site_coverage). Signed contracts are explicit blocks at contract terms: Microsoft/Vineland 300 MW, $3.48B/yr 2027-30 + $1.28B 2031 (remaining ~$15.2B of $17.4B); Meta-2025 ~50 MW, $0.58B/yr to 2030 ($2.9B 6-K); Meta-2026 dedicated $12B on 130 MW (Mantsala 2 70 + Lappeenranta 60, owned), $1.0B 2027, $2.4B/yr 2028-31, $1.4B 2032; Meta backstop up to $15B valued at a $13.5B floor on 150 MW at Highridge PA, 2027-32; Q2-26 neolab deals ~$2.0B/yr 2027-28 on ~90 MW (Bethune/Beit Shemesh). After each term the same GPUs re-lease on the round-3 decay curve (1.00/0.80/0.60/0.48/0.42/0.36/0.30 of launch) and are refreshed at age 6 into merchant cohorts. Uncontracted MW: each under-construction/pipeline tranche probability-weighted (0.50-0.95, expected 3.6 GW by 2031 vs 5 GW target), net of its capex: owned sites $30.75M/MW ($18.75M servers + $12M facility) with $1.3M/MW power+site opex and $0.6M/MW facility sustaining capex; leased sites $20M/MW ($18.75M + $1.25M fit-out) with $3.0M/MW power+colo. Merchant launch $18.75M per earning MW, 35% on 5-yr / 65% on 2-yr terms, 90% of MW earning, 27% variable cost, $0.375M/MW repair from age 3. Discounting: contracted IG cash flows 8.0% (delivered: Microsoft, Meta-2025) and 8.75% (Meta-2026 dedicated and backstop, not yet delivered), unrated Q2-26 deals 10.0%, everything else (post-contract, merchant, pipeline, terminal) WACC 12.1%, g 3%. EV $36.3B at 1/1/27 - $3.7B net debt + $3.5B investments - $7.64B out-of-the-money converts = /322M, rolled 9 months at 12.7% = $97 (single-rate 12.1%: $93). Sensitivities (split rate): life 5/7 yrs on the same curve $106/$72; glut curve (floor 0.20) $81; launch $16.75M/$20.75M $26/$167; 5-yr share 20%/50% $63/$130; owned facility capex $10M/$13.5M $122/$78; server capex +$3M/MW $45; tranche probabilities x0.8 $85; WACC 11.1%/13.1% $125/$75; ERP 5.0% $67; contracted rates +/-100bp to 9.0/9.75/11.0% or 6.5/7.5/9.0% $96/$98.

inputs_detail.value: Energized and 2026 deliveries 1.0; Bethune 2027 0.85; Israel 0.85; Tallinn 0.90; Harlow 0.90; Lappeenranta 0.75-0.85; Highridge 0.85 (2027), 0.65-0.75 later; Independence 0.80 (2027) falling to 0.55 (2031); Birmingham 0.70-0.75; Madrid/Newport 0.80; UK-4th 0.60; AIB 0.85; Oklahoma 0.50; unallocated 0.9 GW 0.50; asset-light and Palantir 0 MW
inputs_detail.derivation: Higher for signed leases and host-funded shells already being built, lower for later phases that need grid power not yet delivered (Independence additional power early 2029), for sites with pending litigation or timing conflicts (Birmingham), single-source MW (Madrid, UK-4th) and sites with no disclosed MW (Oklahoma, the unallocated ~1 GW). Expected capacity 3.6 GW by 2031 vs the 5 GW contracted-power target: a skeptic's haircut for execution and financing.

inputs_detail.value: 300 MW; $17.4B TCV over 5 yrs through 2031; ~$2.2B recognised 2025-26, remaining $3.48B/yr 2027-30 + $1.28B 2031; Microsoft pays Nebius; leased build-to-suit ($3.0M/MW power+lease)
inputs_detail.derivation: $11.6M/MW-yr at 300 MW (derived). 300 MW (Nebius PR) chosen over 315/350 MW (secondary) because the contract value is tied to the company's figure; any Phase-2 MW sit in the unallocated bucket. All tranches delivered by Aug-2026, so the termination-for-late-delivery right has lapsed in practice.

inputs_detail.value: 2025: $2.9B, ~50 MW in the existing fleet, $0.58B/yr to 2030. 2026 dedicated: $12B on ~130 MW (Mantsala 2 70 + Lappeenranta 60), tranches from early 2027, $2.4B/yr run-rate. Backstop: up to $15B; Meta must buy unsold capacity on specified clusters for 5 yrs from deployment; valued as a $13.5B floor on 150 MW at Highridge (2027-32). Meta pays Nebius in all three
inputs_detail.derivation: $2.9B (6-K) chosen over ~$3B (letter) as the filing figure. MW are derived assuming Meta pays ~$18-18.5M/MW (near the merchant launch price); fewer MW would mean less capex and more value. The backstop is a floor under revenue, so I value it at a 10% haircut to 'up to $15B' for late-delivery discounts and partial take-up; third-party sales above the floor are not credited. Fixes flags F3 and F4: Meta is no longer booked in the legacy fleet at $12M/MW and no longer also justifies a 50% 5-yr share in new cohorts.

inputs_detail.value: >$4B across Reflection AI, Cohere, an AI neolab and a quant firm; $20-25M/MW; ~90 MW at Bethune/Beit Shemesh; $2.0B/yr 2027-28
inputs_detail.derivation: $4B over a ~2-yr average term at $22.5M/MW gives ~90 MW; ~70% carry prepayments of 50-60% of capex, already in the $9.5B deferred revenue.

inputs_detail.input: Merchant launch price per earning MW
inputs_detail.derivation: Supervisor asked to anchor it: Q2-26 ACV $20-25M (midpoint $22.5M) x ~83% for ramp, idle time and the lower price hyperscale buyers pay (Meta-2026 ~$18-18.5M derived, Microsoft $11.6M). Unchanged from round 3.
With Microsoft and Meta now modelled explicitly, the remaining capacity is sold to mid-term buyers (1-3 yrs per the Q2 letter); 35% keeps room for further hyperscaler deals. 20%/50% gives $63/$130.

inputs_detail.input: Post-contract price curve (share of launch price by age 0-6)
inputs_detail.derivation: H100 fell ~50% in the ~18 months after its successor shipped and then flattened near $2.80, ~42% of its 2H23 level after 3 years (source 39); A100 rents 23-39% of launch at ~6 years (sources 40, 41); Ornn prices old and new chips at ~$3 per PFLOP-hr, so old chips reprice with the cost of compute rather than to scrap. The research's 25-35%/yr decline for 2-3 years then a floor is the shape used. In my curve the price stays above the cash cost (power+colo+site ops ~$3.0M/MW, ~16% of launch) at every age, so the tail generates cash until the refresh.

inputs_detail.value: Owned (Independence, Highridge, Birmingham, Lappeenranta, Mantsala 1/2): $30.75M ($18.75M servers/network + $12M facility, 20-yr life) + $0.6M/MW-yr facility sustaining; leased/colo: $20.0M ($18.75M + $1.25M fit-out); 40% the year before connection
inputs_detail.derivation: Fixes flag F2 on the capex side. C&W 2026: ~$11.3M/MW hyperscale shell-and-core globally and $17.6M per MW (excluding chips) for modern US/Canada builds (critical-MW basis, ~ $13.5M per gross MW at PUE 1.3); I take $12M. Blended at ~75% owned this is ~$28M/MW vs round 3's $25M, consistent with C&W's +21% cost inflation.

inputs_detail.value: Owned: $1.3M per earning MW (power ~$0.9M at PUE 1.3 and $0.08/kWh + ~$0.4M site ops); leased: $3.0M (adds ~$1.8M colo at ~$150/kW-month, incl. 10-12 yr leases at Harlow and AIB as fixed costs); both + 27% of revenue + $0.375M/MW repair from age 3
inputs_detail.derivation: Fixes flag F2: round 3 charged a colocation-style $3.0M/MW on owned MW and also charged facility capex. Fleet EBITDA margin now ~55% (2027) and 58-60% from 2028 because most new MW are owned; the owned saving is largely paid back by the $12M facility capex and sustaining capex, so F2 nets to ~+$1/share (round-3 treatment $97).

inputs_detail.value: Base 6 years (unchanged): servers refreshed at age 6 at $18.75M/MW (40% prior year), resale at 15% of launch x 60% GPU share x 75%; same-curve sensitivities 5y $106 / 7y $72
inputs_detail.derivation: Fact-checked company lives: Nebius 5 (from Jan-2026), CoreWeave 6, IREN 5. Supervisor asked for life sensitivities on one fixed curve: on it a 5-yr refresh is worth ~$10 more than 6, so 6 is the conservative base; 7 loses value because old GPUs earn ~30% of launch while repair and fixed costs continue.

inputs_detail.value: 8.0% delivered IG (Microsoft AAA, Meta-2025 AA-); 8.75% undelivered IG (Meta-2026 dedicated and backstop); 10.0% unrated Q2-26 deals
inputs_detail.derivation: Anchor: the $775M facility secured on an IG contract at SOFR+2.50% = 6.37% floating today (SOFR 3.87%); on a 5-yr fixed basis (5-yr UST 5.09%, swap ~5.0%) ~7.5%. Add ~50bp for Nebius operating/termination risk on delivered contracts -> 8.0%, and ~125bp for completion risk (late-delivery fee discounts) on undelivered Meta clusters -> 8.75%. Meta's own 2031 notes at 4.55% cap the pure credit component. Unrated AI labs: between 8.75% and the 12.1% WACC; prepayments cover 50-60% of capex on ~70% of deals, but CoreWeave unsecured at ~11.6% shows what weak AI credit costs -> 10%.

inputs_detail.value: ~$9.5B at YE26, unwinding ~$1.5B/yr to ~$5B by 2030 (company-level, at WACC)
inputs_detail.derivation: $5.98B at 6/30/26 plus the rest of >$9B of 2026 prepayments less recognition; recognising revenue on prepaid contracts without new cash is a drag, kept at WACC.
Dutch statutory rate ~25.8%; losses to date are carried forward.
10-yr UST on 2026-09-30 (FRED).
Supervisor round-2 correction: Damodaran implied ERP 4.14% on Sep 1, 2026 (was 4.3%). At 5.0% the WACC is 13.5% and the DCF is $62.
Reported 5-yr beta 1.46 is distorted by the 2022-24 suspension; 106% realized vol and neocloud cyclicality justify ~1.8 -> cost of equity 12.7% at a 4.14% ERP.

~92% equity at 12.7%, ~8% straight debt at ~4.5% after tax (SOFR+2.50% secured facility; low-coupon converts). CoreWeave unsecured at ~11.6% YTM shows the marginal unsecured cost is far higher, which is a reason not to lower the WACC. Kept for all non-contracted cash flows as the brief requires; strictly, carving low-risk contracted flows out of a firm-level beta leaves a riskier residual (residual at 13.1%: split DCF $75).
Nominal long-run growth below the 5.29% risk-free yield; applied from 2032 as +3%/yr capacity beyond the inventory (worth ~$0 at WACC: new merchant MW earn about their cost of capital).

Cash ~$4.35B at YE26 ($8.04B at 6/30 + $5.69B net Aug notes proceeds + ~$5B H2 operating cash incl. prepayments - ~$14.4B H2 capex) vs $5.75B Aug-2026 notes (supervisor correction from $5.0B; conversion $313-325, out of the money) + $0.78B secured facility + $1.51B leases. The extra $0.75B of debt is matched by cash, so net debt is unchanged.

Supervisor round-2 correction: book value $1,606.7M (ClickHouse $1,517.7M) understates the stake after ClickHouse's ~$15B Jan-2026 round confirmed in the Q2 letter; ~$3.5B after a haircut for an unverified stake size, liquidation preferences and illiquidity.

inputs_detail.value: 322M shares with Sep-25 and Mar-26 converts as $7.64B debt (369M if all converts are in the money)
inputs_detail.derivation: 369M fully diluted when all converts are in the money: 271.86M A+B outstanding (6/30/26) + 15.8M Aug-2026 exchange shares + 21.07M NVIDIA pre-funded warrants + ~50.5M convert shares (65.4M anti-dilutive at Q2 less ~15.6M retired in the Aug exchange: ~3.9M Jun-25 remainder, 22.8M Sep-25 at $138.75, 23.8M Mar-26 at ~$181-183) + 10.0M awards. The DCF value (~$101) is below both conversion prices, so in the DCF the Sep-25 ($3.3B accreted) and Mar-26 ($4.34B) notes are debt and the count is 322M.

inputs_detail.value: Gordon on the average FCFF of 2045-2050 (one refresh cycle) at WACC; all contracts end by 2032, so the terminal is entirely merchant
inputs_detail.derivation: Terminal value ~$10B of the $36B EV.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM EBITDA at Oct-2027 ~$10.2B (NTM revenue ~$20.4B x 50%) x 9.0x = EV $91.8B; less $11.4B net debt, plus $3.5B investments = $83.9B / 402M = ~$209, cut ~4% to $200 for funding/execution risk.

inputs_detail.derivation: Site model: 2027 $12.9B, 2028 $27.7B; Q4-27 + Q1-Q3-28 with a linear quarterly ramp ~$22.1B, cut ~8% for slippage. Implies exit-2027 ARR ~$17B vs BNP's ~$22B.

Model says ~58% in 2028 once owned capacity (lower opex) dominates, but peers' multiples are set on lease-heavy margins (CoreWeave ~58% mature, NBIS AI cloud 49.7% Q2-26), so I use 50% to avoid crediting F2 twice.

CoreWeave EV ~$95B is ~7x 2027 EBITDA as it ramps; 9x gives NBIS a premium for lower leverage and faster growth. I don't go higher because CoreWeave's ~11.6% bond yield shows credit markets are pricing neocloud risk.

inputs_detail.derivation: $3.7B at start-2027 + half of a ~$15.3B Jan-Sep 2027 funding gap (site model FCFF -$16.5B for 2027, vs -$21B in round 3, because tranches are probability-weighted) funded with secured debt against the >$40B of contracts; investments ~$3.5B (supervisor).
369M fully diluted (all converts in the money at a ~$200 value) + ~33M new shares for the other half of the ~$15.3B gap at ~$230 (round 3: 42M). The Aug-26 notes stay out of the money.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Oct-2027 ~$20.4B x 4.5x = EV $91.8B; less $11.4B net debt, plus $3.5B investments = $83.9B / 402M = ~$209, cut to $200.

inputs_detail.derivation: Site model: 2027 $12.9B, 2028 $27.7B; Q4-27 + Q1-Q3-28 with a linear quarterly ramp ~$22.1B, cut ~8% for slippage. Implies exit-2027 ARR ~$17B vs BNP's ~$22B.

CoreWeave ~4.9x EV/NTM sales today (~3.8x 2027E). By Oct-2027 NBIS NTM growth slows from triple digits to ~75%, so 4.5x is a modest premium to the peer, discounted for Redburn's GPU-pricing and financing-spread concerns.

inputs_detail.derivation: $3.7B at start-2027 + half of a ~$15.3B Jan-Sep 2027 funding gap (site model FCFF -$16.5B for 2027, vs -$21B in round 3, because tranches are probability-weighted) funded with secured debt against the >$40B of contracts; investments ~$3.5B (supervisor).
369M fully diluted (all converts in the money at a ~$200 value) + ~33M new shares for the other half of the ~$15.3B gap at ~$230 (round 3: 42M). The Aug-26 notes stay out of the money.

bear.story: Neocloud economics revert, as Redburn argues: GPU rents fall as supply catches up and Rubin arrives, mid-term (1-3 yr) contracts reprice toward the $12M/MW fleet base, and hyperscalers in-source. Credit tightens: CoreWeave-style 11-12% unsecured yields and a weak convert market force dilutive equity at low prices. The 2027 guide lands near the low consensus (~$9-10B). The stock re-rates to ~6-7x forward EBITDA and trades below the $138.75 Sep-25 conversion price. My DCF at fleet-base yields is ~$10-60. GPU-life angle: if Rubin supply creates a glut, post-contract rents fall to ~20% of launch and the 2-yr mid-term half of the fleet reprices fast. My DCF then drops to ~$35, and to ~$28 if only 30% of capacity sits on 5-yr contracts. Round-4 site angle: if later phases at Independence/Highridge slip (tranche probabilities x0.8) and new MW cost C&W's full $17.6M/MW facility price, the DCF falls to ~$75-85, and the only firm value is ~$29/share of Microsoft/Meta contract-term cash flow.

base.story: Execution holds: ~1 GW added in 2027, 2027 revenue ~$12B, margins near 50%, yields settle a little above the 2026 fleet base. The ~$20B 2027 funding gap is met with prepayments, secured debt and some ATM/converts (~40M+ new shares). The multiple compresses from ~7x to ~4.5-5x forward sales, so the stock ends modestly below today, above my $159 fair value because the market keeps paying for growth optionality. In the base case the GPU-life evidence (A100s still renting at 6 yrs, CoreWeave re-contracting H100s within 5%) supports a 6-yr economic life with front-loaded rents, which, with the round-4 site-by-site build and split discounting, leaves the DCF at ~$97.

bull.story: The BNP case: Q2-type $20-25M/MW deals (and >$40M short-term deals) persist, exit-2027 ARR approaches $22B, prepayments limit dilution, and the formal 2027 guide resets estimates higher. At an $18M steady yield my own DCF gives ~$260; with a premium multiple and a squeeze off ~20% short interest, analyst highs of $399-415 are reachable. Site view: all named campuses delivered on schedule (probabilities 1.0) gives a DCF ~$119 before any price upside; a 50% long-term share gives $130.

thesis_break_reason: A close below ~$115 (about half of spot, below the $138.75 Sep-25 conversion price; equity ~$42B on ~369M diluted shares, under 2x my 2027-28 revenue path) would most likely mean something fundamental broke rather than 100%-vol noise: new-deal $/MW rolling back toward the $12M fleet base, a slip in >1 GW 2027 deployment, a cut or delay at Microsoft/Meta (top three customers 59% of Q2 revenue), or the financing window closing (unrated issuer, neocloud spreads already ~11-12%), forcing equity at depressed prices. Added in round 3: evidence that expiring 2-yr mid-term contracts are re-pricing below ~50% of launch (the glut path), since half of each cohort reprices within 2-3 years. Round 4: also a delay of Meta-2026 tranches at Mantsala 2/Lappeenranta or of Highridge's 260 MW by Oct-2027, which would put the IG-contracted floor at risk.

More ATM/convertible/ABS financing for 2027 capex of ~$25B+ (Aug-2026 $5B convert caused a -10% day)
YE2026 milestones: 0.8-1 GW connected and 5 GW contracted power
FY2026 results and 20-F (depreciation policy, RPO conversion, concentration, convert accounting)

key_uncertainties: Merchant launch price and contract mix on capacity not yet sold (~85% of 2030 MW): launch $16.75-20.75M gives a DCF of $26-167; 5-yr share 20-50% gives $63-130
Build cost of owned campuses: facility $10-13.5M/MW gives $122-78; servers +$3M/MW gives $45 (C&W puts 2026 costs +21% vs late 2024)
Delivery of the ~3.4 GW under construction (Independence power by early 2029, Birmingham lawsuits, Highridge 260 MW by Oct-2027): probabilities x0.8 gives $85
Funding >$20B/yr of capex: dilution (402M diluted shares by Oct-27 in my base) and access to secured credit (SOFR+250bp so far) while unsecured neocloud paper yields ~11-12%
Customer concentration: Microsoft and Meta are ~$11B of 2028 contracted revenue; top three customers 59% of Q2-26 revenue
GPU economic life and re-lease path: same-curve 5y/7y $106/$72; glut curve $81
Discount rates: WACC 11.1-13.1% gives $125-75; contracted rates +/-100bp only move the DCF ~$1-2
reasoning: Round 4 (site inventory and split discounting). I rebuilt the DCF from the checked site inventory so each site appears once: signed contracts are explicit blocks at their own terms (Microsoft/Vineland $3.48B/yr to 2031; Meta-2025 $0.58B/yr to 2030; Meta-2026 $12B on ~130 MW in Finland from 2027; Meta's up-to-$15B purchase obligation valued as a $13.5B floor on 150 MW at Highridge; Q2-26 neolab deals $2B/yr 2027-28). Every other tranche of every site is probability-weighted (0.50-0.95) and charged its own capex and opex by ownership. That fixes flags F1-F4, F6 and F9: owned MW pay power+site opex only but carry facility capex at C&W 2026 costs; Meta is no longer booked in the legacy fleet at $12M; the YE26 earning base is 0.65 GW, not 0.9 GW connected. The supervisor's round-3 points are applied: life sensitivities on one fixed curve (5y $106 > 6y $97 > 7y $72) and the launch price anchored to Q2 ACV less ramp. Discounting: contract-term IG cash flows at 8.0% (delivered) / 8.75% (undelivered), anchored on the SOFR+2.50% secured facility (6.37% floating, ~7.5% fixed) plus operating or completion risk; unrated Q2 deals at 10%; everything else at 12.1%. Result: single-rate DCF $93, split-rate $97 (round 3 $104). The split adds only ~$4 because the ~$32B of IG contracts nets to ~$13.6B of cash after opex, tax and the Meta build capex, all received by 2032. The skeptic's finding is that the explicit contracts are worth ~$29/share, while the rest of the DCF rests on unsold capacity at ~$18.75M/MW and on campuses that are not yet powered. Multiples legs are unchanged at ~$200 (lower NTM revenue offset by a smaller funding gap, so less net debt and dilution). Blended fair value $159 vs $159.8: unchanged, so scenarios, both ladders and the $115 thesis break stay; the stories now cite the site-level drivers. Research this round: FRED SOFR and 5-yr UST fetches, one search (C&W 2026 data-center cost guide); site and contract facts come from the checked inventory and the filings it cites. I found no inventory fact that needed correcting; where sources conflict I chose: Vineland 300 MW (company PR), Meta-2025 $2.9B (6-K), Bethune leased, Birmingham operational 2027. Round-2/3 trace retained: lognormal mixture of bear $105 (30%, sigma 0.5), base $215 (45%, 0.35), bull $400 (25%, 0.4), median ~$210, P(>= spot) 0.43; neocloud credit stress (CoreWeave ~11.6% YTM, CDS ~855bp) fattens the left tail.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Signed contracts at contract price for their terms (Microsoft to 2031, Meta-2025 to 2030, Meta-2026 dedicated and backstop 2027-32, Q2-26 deals 2027-28); unsigned cohorts 35% on 5-yr / 65% on 2-yr. After expiry the price as a share of launch by age 0-6 is 1.00, 0.80, 0.60, 0.48, 0.42, 0.36, 0.30, above cash cost at every age. Refresh at age 6 at full server cost ($18.75M/MW) with resale at 15% of launch x 60% x 75%. Life sensitivities now hold this curve fixed (5y truncates it at 0.36; 7y extends it flat at 0.30).
gpu_life.note: Same approach as round 3 with the supervisor's fix: 5y/7y now on one fixed curve ($106/$72); curve sensitivity shown separately (glut floor 0.20: $81). On the fixed curve a 5-yr refresh maximises value; I keep 6 as a conservative base given Nebius books 5 and CoreWeave 6 (fact-checked). Site rebuild and split discounting: DCF $104 -> $97 (single-rate $93).

discounting.basis: Contracted IG cash flows inside signed terms: 8.0% for delivered contracts (Microsoft AAA to 2031; Meta-2025 Aa3 to 2030) and 8.75% for undelivered Meta-2026 dedicated and backstop clusters (2027-32). Anchor: the $775M facility secured on one IG contract at SOFR+2.50% (6.37% floating with SOFR 3.87%; ~7.5% fixed-equivalent with the 5-yr UST at 5.09%), plus ~50bp operating/termination risk, or ~125bp when completion risk remains; Meta's 4.55% 2031 notes cap the pure credit part. Unrated Q2-26 neolab/quant contracts (2027-28): 10.0%, between the IG rate and WACC; prepayments fund 50-60% of capex on ~70% of them, but CoreWeave unsecured yields ~11.6%. Post-contract, merchant, pipeline and terminal: WACC 12.1%. Contract-term cash flows are worth ~$8.5B at the split rates vs ~$7.5B at WACC, so the split adds ~$3.6/share: the ~$32B headline TCV turns into only ~$13.6B of net cash after opex, tax and the capex of the undelivered clusters, and it runs off within ~2.5-3 yrs on average. Residual WACC kept at 12.1% as instructed although the remaining equity is riskier once contracts are carved out (13.1%: $75).
